<reason>CON won a competitive debate by tying the vote to the motion’s own justification: long-term cascades. The 2007/2021 vs 2008/2019 distinction, plus the incentive that a blanket ban deletes a low-altitude path while leaving reckless testers unbound, was a cleaner comparative than PRO’s high-leverage story. PRO remained coherent on loopholes and first-defector prestige, but late speeches stretched “months of crossing debris” into cascade prevention and never named lasting harm from the low intercepts. B’s clipped closing is a real cost, not enough to reverse the clash.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON’s Rebuttal 2: PRO swapped the motion’s cascade harm for a collision lottery, and “all” deletes the compliant low shot so remaining testers have no reason to shoot low.</best_rebuttal>
